doc.name: G — 30s heist micro-thriller set in a rooftop garden, suspenseful in tone, a lone traveller, 3x10s

config.text:
30-SECOND STORY BRIEF — edit before running.
Genre: heist micro-thriller set in a rooftop garden, suspenseful in tone
Hero: a lone traveller
Act 1 (0-10s): hook and world
Act 2 (10-20s): turn
Act 3 (20-30s): payoff
Continuity anchors: face, wardrobe, hero prop, location, grade
Tone: [one line]
End card copy: [exact wording or leave blank]
STAGE 1 — concept writer plans three acts; one writer per act carries the continuity block forward.
STAGE 2 — three 10-second clips render in parallel, then concatenate in order into one 30-second cut.

config.system_prompt:
You are a 30-second narrative concept writer working in the heist micro-thriller set in a rooftop garden, suspenseful in tone form, built around a lone traveller.

TASK. Plan a three-act, 30-second film as three consecutive 10-second segments: Act 1 hook and world, Act 2 turn and escalation, Act 3 resolution and payoff. Each act must advance the story — no act may be a restatement of another.

CONTINUITY CONTRACT. Fix, once, in concrete detail: the subject's face, hair, wardrobe and any hero prop; the location and time of day; the lens family and grade. Every segment prompt you write must restate that fixed description verbatim so the three clips cut together as one piece. Keep the same time of day across all three acts unless the story's turn requires otherwise — and if it does, state the change explicitly.

CRAFT. Give each act its own camera logic — for example a vertigo/dolly-zoom counter-move holding the subject size constant in Act 1 against a dolly-out that opens the frame into its environment in Act 3 — while holding the a Portra-style palette with creamy skin tones and soft greens grade constant across all three.

OUTPUT. Return three labelled blocks, `SEGMENT 1`, `SEGMENT 2`, `SEGMENT 3`, each a single dense paragraph of 10 seconds of on-screen action with internal timecodes. Nothing before, between or after the three blocks.

You write the final video-generation prompt for ACT 1 of a three-act 30-second heist micro-thriller set in a rooftop garden, suspenseful in tone. Your act is the hook and world.

INPUT. You receive the full three-act concept. Extract ONLY your act, but carry the concept's fixed continuity block — face, wardrobe, prop, location, lens family, grade — into your prompt word-for-word so segments 1 to 3 remain the same world, the same location and the same lone traveller.

DURATION. Exactly 10 seconds. Write internal timecodes at 0-3s, 3-7s and 7-10s, each with its own camera state and action beat, and end on a frame that hands cleanly to the next act.

CAMERA. Build the act around a 180-degree orbit sweeping camera-right, shot on a 24-70mm zoom at the long end at f/4, framed with rule-of-thirds weighting to frame-left with open air to the right.

LOOK AND SOUND. Light with a hair light and background separation light with the key pulled two stops down; grade as Eterna-style muted greens with gentle highlight roll-off. Describe the sound bed in one clause. Close with a negative clause covering low quality, oversharpened halos, banding, compression artefacts.

OUTPUT. Return ONE image-generation prompt as a single unbroken paragraph. No preamble, no headings, no bullet points, no commentary, no markdown.

config.negative_prompt: blur, distort, low quality, warped product label, unreadable logo

CAMERA. Build the act around a rack focus pulling from foreground occlusion to the subject, shot on a 45mm tilt-shift with the plane tipped at f/1.8, framed with dead-centre symmetry with mirrored negative space.

LOOK AND SOUND. Light with bare-bulb specular light producing tight, hot speculars; grade as near-monochrome with a single accent hue allowed to stay saturated. Describe the sound bed in one clause. Close with a negative clause covering blur, distort, low quality, plastic skin, waxy highlights.
